bodh-p01.speaker: Kṣemarāja (11th c., Abhinavagupta's disciple)
bodh-p01.question: What is consciousness, and how does it become the embodied experiencer?
premises: Salutation (vv. 1): oṃ namaḥ netrāya namaḥ śivāya satataṃ pañcakṛtyavidhāyine | cidānandaghanasvātmaparamārthāvabhāsine — Oṃ, salutation to Netra, salutation to Śiva, constantly, maker of the five acts, manifester of supreme self-bliss.

Core thesis (v. 2): citiḥ svatantrā viśvasya hetur ity abhidhīyate — consciousness is free and the cause of the universe, thus it is called. Svātantryarūpā jñātā ca siddhīr vā saṃprayacchate — of the form of freedom, the knower, and bestows powers or liberation.

Unfolding (v. 2): sā svabhittau svecchayaiva viśvasyonmīlanāya ca | nānānurūpavaicitryād grāhyagrāhakabhedataḥ — she, in her own ground, by her own will, for the unfolding of the universe; from various corresponding variety, from difference of object and subject.

Variety (v. 2): viśvasya tasya vaicitryaṃ grāhyabhedena saṃsthitam | nānāvaicitryayogena cottamādhamasaṅkhyayā — the universe's variety is established by difference of objects; by variety of varieties and by number of high and low.

Contraction into mind (v. 2): citisaṅkocanāc cittaṃ cetano 'pi maheśvaraḥ | vaṭadhanikāvat tatra viśvarūpaṃ ca tad viduḥ — from contraction of consciousness, mind; consciousness also, the great lord; like a banyan seed, there, the universal form, and that, know.

Consciousness and mind (v. 2): caitanyam ātmano rūpaṃ śuddham atyantanirmalam | tad eva niyamāsaktaṃ cittaṃ cid abhidhīyate — consciousness is the form of the self, pure, extremely immaculate; that same, attached to rules, mind, consciousness, is called.

Rest and contraction (v. 2): arthonmukhatayā saṃvic citte viśrāntim āgatā | saṅkocātmapradhānatvāc citiś cittaṃ vidur budhāḥ — with object-directedness, awareness in mind has arrived at rest; from contraction as self-predominance, consciousness, mind, know the wise.

Māyā-knower (v. 2): māyāpramātā cidrūpas tanmayatvena dehinām | vartate viṣayāsaktaḥ sadvivekavivarjitaḥ — māyā-knower, consciousness-formed, as identity with that, of embodied beings, exists, attached to objects, devoid of true discrimination.

Contracted self (v. 2): sadaikaḥ pratithaś cittaṃ kalāsattvaguṇādibhiḥ | saptapramatṛkatvena ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṅkhyayā — one constant, primary, mind, by kala, sattva, guṇa etc.; by seven knowerhood, by thirty-six principles.

Great lord (v. 2): ekaḥ sarvagataḥ śuddhaḥ sambodhātmā maheśvaraḥ | saivāhantāparijñānān muktiḥ karatale sthitā — one, all-pervading, pure, of the nature of supreme awareness, the great lord; from non-recognition of that I-ness, liberation is situated in the palm.
bodh-p01.inference: Consciousness (citi) is free (svatantra) and the cause (hetu) of the universe. It manifests as supreme self-bliss (cidānandaghana), while in its own ground it unfolds variety by will (svecchā) and difference of subject and object (grāhyagrāhakabheda). Contracted into mind (citta) and māyā-bound knowership (māyāpramātā), the same consciousness appears bound, yet liberation (mukti) remains at hand (karatale sthitā) through recognizing that I-ness (ahaṃtā). The text's core move: liberation is not creating something new but recognizing what one already is — the original freedom of consciousness. The banyan seed analogy: the seed contains the whole tree; similarly, the contracted mind contains the universal form.
bodh-p01.conclusion: Consciousness is free (svatantra) and the cause of the universe. It unfolds variety from its own ground by will. Contracted into mind, it appears bound, yet liberation is at hand through recognizing I-ness (ahaṃtā). Key: citisaṅkocanāc cittaṃ (mind is consciousness contracted) and saivāhantāparijñānān muktiḥ karatale sthitā (liberation at hand from non-recognition of I-ness).
bodh-p01.theorem: citi = svatantra hetu of viśva; citta = citi-saṅkoca (contraction); mukti = ahaṃtā-parijñāna (recognition of I-ness), karatale sthitā.
unresolved_terms: banyan seed analogy (vaṭadhanikāvat) — T1 gloss renders 'like a banyan seed, there, the universal form'; Sanskrit compressed
seven knowerhoods (saptapramatṛ) and thirty-six principles (ṣaṭtriṃśattattva) — standard Trika cosmology, not enumerated here
text is a yogaśāstra (yoga treatise) — practical, not just philosophical; esoteric second sense present but less emphasized than Paramārthasāra
bodh-p01.next_pressure: L2: salutation → core thesis (citi is svatantra, hetu of viśva) → unfolding (svecchā, grāhyagrāhakabheda) → variety (grāhyabheda, ottamādhamasaṅkhyā) → contraction into mind (citisaṅkocanāc cittaṃ) → consciousness and mind (caitanyam ātmano rūpaṃ, tad eva niyamāsaktaṃ cittaṃ) → rest and contraction (saṃvic citte viśrāntim āgatā) → māyā-knower (māyāpramātā) → contracted self (sadaikaḥ pratithaś cittaṃ) → great lord (ekaḥ sarvagataḥ śuddhaḥ sambodhātmā maheśvaraḥ) → liberation at hand (muktiḥ karatale sthitā). Key: v. 2's citisaṅkocanāc cittaṃ and saivāhantāparijñānān muktiḥ karatale sthitā. Tone: scholastic-practical (yogaśāstra). Two-level structure: pragmatic (saṃsārin, contracted) and ultimate (śaktīśa, expanded).

bodh-p02.speaker: Kṣemarāja (11th c.)
bodh-p02.question: How does liberation-glory proceed? What is the relation between contraction and expansion?
premises: v11: pramātṛsaptakatvena ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṅkhyayā | bhāvitaḥ sa maheśāno mokṣalakṣmīḥ pravartate — cultivated by seven knowerhoods and thirty-six principles, he, Maheśāna, liberation-glory proceeds.

v12: tadbhūmikā darśanādyāḥ sarvā eva na saṃśayaḥ | bhūmikāḥ kṛtrimā yadvan naṭo gṛhṇāti svecchayā — its stages, perceptions etc., all indeed not doubt; stages artificial, just as an actor assumes by own will.
v13: tadvad eva cidānandasvecchocchalitabṛṃhitaḥ | ātmā gṛhṇāti vipulā darśanādyā vibhūtayaḥ — likewise indeed, expanded by bliss-will, the self assumes vast perceptions etc. powers.

v14: cidvatsvaśaktisaṅkocāt saṃsāre malināyate | apūrṇo 'smīti vividhair malaiḥ sa malinīkṛtaḥ — from contraction of own power, in saṃsāra, becomes impure; 'I am incomplete' thus; by various malas, he is defiled.

v15: māyīyāṇavakārmākhyair vyāpako 'pi jagadvibhuḥ | vyāpī yadvan mahādevaḥ kroti pañcakṛtyatām | tadvad evāyam ātmāpi kurute śaktimohitaḥ — named māyīya-āṇava-kārma, all-pervading also, lord of world, all-pervading; just as great god does five acts, likewise this self also does, deluded by power.

v16: śaktimohitaḥ śakto vikāsāc chaktīśo gīyate | saṅkocanāt saṅkocitaḥ saṃsārīty abhidhīyate — deluded by power, capable; from expansion, lord of powers is said; from contraction, contracted, as saṃsārin is called.

v17: māyā rūpaṃ hi yat kiṃcid ālokayitum udyatā | sādhyasṛṣṭiṃ vijānīyād anyā śaktiḥ sthitir matā — māyā is form indeed; somewhat, to perceive, intent; created creation should know; other power, preservation is considered.

v18: saṃhārāt saṃhṛtā devī cidaikye 'nugraho mataḥ | tadekasārāprathanāt tirodhānābhidhīyate — from dissolution, withdrawn, goddess; in unity of consciousness, grace is considered; from manifestation of that essence, concealment is called.

v19: itthaṃ sadā saṃnihitaḥ pañcavāhavidhiḥ kramāt | jñātaś cintāmaṇir asāv ajñānāt kāṣṭaloṣṭavat — thus always present, the fivefold process in order, known; the wish-jewel, that; from ignorance, like wood and clod.
bodh-p02.inference: Liberation-glory (mokṣalakṣmī) proceeds through stages (bhūmikā). The self assumes vast powers by its own will (svecchā), like an actor. From contraction (saṅkocana) it becomes a saṃsārin, from expansion (vikāsa) it is lord of powers. The five acts (pañcakṛtya) — creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, grace — are performed by the self even when contracted. The text's core move: the limited knower is not separate from the unlimited knower; the same self, by contraction and expansion, appears as both. The fivefold process (pañcavāha) is always present; the wish-jewel (cintāmaṇi) is known from ignorance (like wood and clod).
bodh-p02.conclusion: Liberation-glory proceeds through stages (bhūmikā). The self assumes vast powers by its own will (svecchā), like an actor. From contraction (saṅkocana) it becomes a saṃsārin; from expansion (vikāsa) it is lord of powers (śaktīśa). The five acts (pañcakṛtya) are performed by the self even when contracted. Key: v. 16 (the same self, by expansion and contraction, appears as both lord of powers and saṃsārin) and v. 15 (even all-pervading, the self performs the five acts, like the great god).
bodh-p02.theorem: mokṣalakṣmī proceeds through bhūmikā; self = śaktīśa (expanded) / saṃsārin (contracted); pañcakṛtya performed by self even when contracted; pañcavāha always present; cintāmaṇi known from ajñāna.
unresolved_terms: seven knowerhoods (saptapramatṛ) and thirty-six tattvas (ṣaṭtriṃśattattva) — standard Trika cosmology, not enumerated
fivefold process (pañcavāha) — creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, grace; implied by v. 18, not explicitly listed

wish-jewel (cintāmaṇi) — the text says 'from ignorance, like wood and clod'; the analogy: the cintāmaṇi is known from ignorance, like wood and clod are known (i.e., the wish-jewel is hidden in ignorance)
bodh-p02.next_pressure: L2: liberation-glory proceeds (v. 11) → its stages are artificial, like an actor (v. 12) → the self assumes vast powers (v. 13) → contraction: impure, defiled (v. 14) → all-pervading yet contracted, like the great god performing five acts (v. 15) → contraction and expansion (v. 16) → māyā is form (v. 17) → dissolution, grace, concealment (v. 18) → fivefold process always present, wish-jewel (v. 19). Key: v. 16 (same self, by expansion/contraction, appears as both) and v. 15 (even all-pervading, performs five acts). Tone: scholastic-practical (yogaśāstra).

bodh-p03.speaker: Kṣemarāja (11th c.)
bodh-p03.question: How is liberation attained? What is the consciousness-fire?
premises: v21: sadvimarśabalenaivaṃ nityaṃ yaḥ pariśīlate | sa muktaḥ sarvabandhebhyo nityānandamayo bhavet — by the power of true reflection, thus always, whoever practices, he is liberated from all bonds, full of eternal bliss, becomes.

v22: cidvahnir grasate so 'yaṃ suprabuddho 'sty asau | yadā tadāsau vimalo jñeyaś cidvahniḥ sarvabhakṣakaḥ — consciousness-fire swallows; that well-awakened is; when then that pure, to be known, consciousness-fire, all-devouring.
v23: etadbalena saṃyukto yogī nirvāṇalakṣaṇaḥ | padaṃ prāpnoti vimalaṃ so 'cirān nātra saṃśayaḥ — by this power, united, yogi marked by liberation, state attains, pure; that soon, no here doubt.

v24: cidvahnir balalābhe 'pi viśvam ābhāti cinmayam | svānandāmṛtakallolam etad ucchalitaṃ bahiḥ — consciousness-fire on gaining power even, universe shines, consciousness-made; wave of self-bliss-nectar, this risen, outside.

v25: tad eva śyānatāṃ yātaṃ bhāvarūpair vibhāvyate | svātmā maheśvaro devaḥ krīḍate parameśvaraḥ — that indeed quiescence gone, by forms of being is manifested; own-self, Maheśvara, god, plays, supreme lord.

v26: iti yaḥ satataṃ vetti sa mukto mocayaty api | sattvavrātaṃ kṣaṇenaiva ghorāt saṃsārabandhanāt — thus whoever constantly knows, he liberated, liberates also multitude of beings in an instant from terrible saṃsāra-bondage.
v27: yaḥ kaścid ānandabalaḥ sa svarūpapadasthitaḥ | iti yasya samullāsollāsitodayaśālinaḥ — whoever, someone, bliss-powered, he established in own state; thus whose exultant-rising.

v28: tasya svarūpaniṣṭhasya vyutthāne 'pi tad arthyate | etat prayatnasāmārthyāj janair evādhigamyate — his fixed in own nature, in distraction even, that is desired; this by effort-power, by people, is attained.

v29: madhyadhāmavikāsāc ca cidānandāt prakāśate | tatprakāśād divyadṛṣṭir jñānarūpā vibhāvyate — from middle-center expansion, and from bliss-consciousness, shines; from its light, divine vision, of form-knowledge, is manifested.

v30: nirmalā suprabhā śuddhā nityānandamayī parā | nirdehacchedajālāpi jñānadṛṣṭir vijṛmbhate — immaculate, radiant, pure, full of eternal bliss, supreme; and net of body-cutting, knowledge-vision expands.
bodh-p03.inference: Liberation (mukti) is by true reflection (sadvimarśa) — not by effort alone but by the power of true reflection. The consciousness-fire (cidvahni) swallows the universe; when well-awakened, it is pure, all-devouring. By this power, the yogi marked by liberation attains the pure state. On gaining power, the consciousness-fire shines; the universe is consciousness-made; the wave of self-bliss-nectar rises outside. That (the wave) gone to quiescence, by forms of being is manifested; own-self is Maheśvara, god, playing, supreme lord. Whoever constantly knows this is liberated and liberates the multitude of beings in an instant from terrible saṃsāra-bondage. Whoever is bliss-powered (ānandabala) is established in own state. His, fixed in own nature, in distraction even, that (state) is desired; this by effort-power, by people, is attained. From middle-center expansion (madhyadhāmavikāsa) and from bliss-consciousness (cidānanda), shines; from its light, divine vision (divyadṛṣṭi), of form-knowledge (jñānarūpā), is manifested. Divine vision is immaculate, radiant, pure, full of eternal bliss, supreme; the net of body-cutting, knowledge-vision expands.
bodh-p03.conclusion: Liberation is by sadvimarśa (true reflection), not by effort alone. The consciousness-fire (cidvahni) swallows the universe; the yogi marked by liberation attains the pure state. The liberated liberates others in an instant. From middle-center expansion and bliss-consciousness, divine vision is manifested — immaculate, radiant, pure, full of eternal bliss, supreme. Key: v. 21 (liberation by true reflection) and v. 26 (the liberated liberates).
bodh-p03.theorem: mukti = sadvimarśabala (power of true reflection); cidvahni (consciousness-fire) swallows viśva; liberated liberates others (kṣaṇenaiva); divyadṛṣṭi (divine vision) from madhyadhāmavikāsa + cidānanda.
unresolved_terms: middle-center expansion (madhyadhāmavikāsa) — T1 gloss renders 'from middle-center expansion'; madhyadhāma refers to central channel (suṣumnā) or heart-center; text does not specify

net of body-cutting (nirdehacchedajāla) — T1 gloss renders 'net of body-cutting'; nirdeha = 'without body' or 'body-transcending'; cheda = 'cutting'; jāla = 'net'. Image: the net that cuts body-bondage
vṛtti by Harabhatta Shastri? No — Pensa 1961 is the standard edition; the text itself is by Kṣemarāja; no separate vṛtti mentioned
bodh-p03.next_pressure: L2: liberation by true reflection (v. 21) → consciousness-fire swallows (v. 22) → by this power, yogi attains pure state (v. 23) → consciousness-fire on gaining power, universe shines (v. 24) → self as Maheśvara playing (v. 25) → the liberated liberates (v. 26) → bliss-powered (v. 27) → fixed in own nature (v. 28) → from middle-center expansion, divine vision (v. 29) → divine vision expands (v. 30). Key: v. 21 (liberation by true reflection) and v. 26 (the liberated liberates). Tone: scholastic-practical (yogaśāstra).

bodh-p04.speaker: Kṣemarāja (11th c.)
bodh-p04.question: What is the method (upāya)? How does middle-center expansion work?
premises: v31: madhyadhāmavikāse tu upāyo balavatsthitiḥ | vikalpakṣayasaṅkocavikāsādyā anekaśaḥ — in middle-center expansion, but, means, powerful state; etc. of thought-decay, contraction, expansion, in many ways.

v32: akiñciccintanād eva vikalpānāṃ kṣayo bhavet | cidbodhād vilasacchaktī raktāsau bhāvamaṇḍale — from thinking of nothing, indeed, of thoughts, decay may be; from consciousness-awareness, playful power, that is attached, in realm of being.

v33: tatrānuraktā divyaughaṃ paśyate vimalātmakam | śaktisaṅkocam etad dhi procyate brahmavādibhiḥ — there attached, divine stream, sees, of pure nature; contraction of power, this indeed is said by brahma-teachers.
v34: ādyantakoṭiviśrāmabindunādalayās tathā | aśaṅkitabhayakrodhabībhatsādiparigrahāḥ — etc. of rest in bindu, nāda at end, beginning; and including fear, anger, disgust etc. grasping.

v35: ity etat kathitaṃ devi madhyadhāmavikāsakam | tatra śakto dinair evaṃ prapnoti parasampadam — thus this said, goddess, middle-center expansion; there capable, in days, thus obtains supreme prosperity.

v36: yo 'ntaḥsamādhisaṃskāraṃ bhramate vimalatviṣām | sa visargabalād eva vimṛśya ca punaḥ punaḥ — who inner samādhi impression wanders, of pure radiance; he by power of emission indeed, reflecting, and again and again.

v37: vyutthāne 'pi yatas tasya svarūpaṃ samprakāśate | yogino bodhaniṣṭhasya nityānandarasasya ca — in distraction even, because his own form fully manifests; of yogi fixed in awareness, of eternal bliss essence.

v38: tat prakāśānandamayī mantravīryopabṛṃhitā | pūrṇāhantācid ity antaḥsamullāsābhiyoginaḥ — that full of manifest bliss, strengthened by mantra-power; consciousness of full I-ness, thus of inner exultation practitioner.

v39: tatrāsau vilasan yogī mantreśvarapade sthitaḥ | tatra śakto vibhur yadvat krīḍate śaktibṛṃhitaḥ — there that sporting yogi situated in status of mantra-lord; there capable, lord, just as plays, expanded by power.

v40: evaṃ svatantratā tasya vyāpakasya jagadvibhoḥ | nānābhedajuṣaś citrapadasthitasyākhaṇḍitā — thus freedom of his, all-pervading, world-lord, enjoying various differences, unbroken in wondrous state.
bodh-p04.inference: Middle-center expansion (madhyadhāmavikāsa) is the method. The upāyas (means) are the contraction-expansion axis: from thinking of nothing (akiñciccintana) thoughts decay; from consciousness-awareness (cidbodha) playful power (vilasacchakti) attaches; the yogi established in own form (svarūpa) is a lord (vibhu) like one expanded by power (śaktibṛṃhita). Freedom (svatantratā) is his — all-pervading, world-lord, enjoying various differences, unbroken in wondrous state. The two-level structure: pragmatic (contracted, saṃsārin) and ultimate (expanded, śaktīśa, vibhu).
bodh-p04.conclusion: Middle-center expansion (madhyadhāmavikāsa) is the method. The upāyas are the contraction-expansion axis. From thinking of nothing, thoughts decay; from consciousness-awareness, playful power attaches. The yogi established in own form is a lord (vibhu) like one expanded by power. Freedom (svatantratā) is his — all-pervading, world-lord, enjoying various differences, unbroken. Key: v. 31 (means is powerful state in middle-center expansion), v. 32 (from thinking of nothing, thoughts decay; from consciousness-awareness, playful power attaches), v. 40 (freedom is his — all-pervading, world-lord).
bodh-p04.theorem: upāya = madhyadhāmavikāsa (middle-center expansion); contraction-expansion axis; freedom (svatantratā) = all-pervading, world-lord, enjoying differences, unbroken.
unresolved_terms: middle-center expansion (madhyadhāmavikāsa) — madhyadhāma refers to central channel (suṣumnā) or heart-center; text does not specify
inner samādhi impression (antaḥsamādhisaṃskāra) — not elaborated in T1
net of body-cutting (nirdehacchedajāla) from p03 — nirdeha = 'without body' or 'body-transcending'; cheda = 'cutting'; jāla = 'net'
bodh-p04.next_pressure: L2: middle-center expansion (v. 31) → from thinking of nothing (v. 32) → divine stream (v. 33) → rest in bindu/nāda (v. 34) → middle-center expansion (v. 35) → inner samādhi impression (v. 36) → in distraction (v. 37) → full of manifest bliss (v. 38) → the yogi as lord (v. 39) → freedom (v. 40). Key: v. 31 (means is powerful state), v. 32 (thinking of nothing → thoughts decay; consciousness-awareness → playful power), v. 40 (freedom is his). Tone: scholastic-practical (yogaśāstra).

bodh-p05.speaker: Kṣemarāja (11th c.)
bodh-p05.question: What is the text's closing word? What is the seal?
premises: v41: etad advayam ity uktaṃ jñānāmṛtam anuttamam | yaḥ pibec chāmyate tasya saṃsāraviṣamūrchanam — this non-dual thus said, nectar of knowledge unsurpassed; whoever may drink, is quenched, his fever of saṃsāra-poison.

v42: bodhollāsavidhāneyaṃ śivaprāpyai mahātmanām | rājñaḥ kṣemābhidhānasya śāstram atyantanirmalam | iti śrīkṣemarājakṛtaṃ bodhavilāsākhyaṃ yogaśāstram — this method of bliss of awareness for attaining Śiva, of great souls; of king named Kṣema, treatise extremely pure, thus composed by Śrī Kṣemarāja, named Bodhavilāsa, yogaśāstra.
bodh-p05.inference: The text closes. The seal: non-dual knowledge (advayam jñānāmṛtam) is unsurpassed; whoever drinks it is quenched of saṃsāra-poison. The method of bliss of awareness (bodhollāsavidhā) is for attaining Śiva (śivaprāpyai), for great souls (mahātmanām). The text is the extremely pure treatise (atyantanirmalam śāstram) of King Kṣema (rājñaḥ kṣemābhidhānasya), composed by Śrī Kṣemarāja (śrīkṣemarājakṛtaṃ), named Bodhavilāsa (bodhavilāsākhyaṃ), a yogaśāstra (yogaśāstram). The text's final word: liberation is not creating something new but recognizing what one already is — the original freedom of consciousness.
bodh-p05.conclusion: The Bodhavilāsa's seal: non-dual knowledge (advayam jñānāmṛtam) is unsurpassed; whoever drinks it is quenched of saṃsāra-poison. The method of bliss of awareness (bodhollāsavidhā) is for attaining Śiva, for great souls. The text is a yogaśāstra by Kṣemarāja. Key: v. 41's etad advayam ity uktaṃ jñānāmṛtam anuttamam (this non-dual knowledge is unsurpassed nectar) and v. 42's bodhollāsavidhāneyaṃ śivaprāpyai mahātmanām (this method of bliss of awareness is for attaining Śiva, for great souls).
bodh-p05.theorem: advayam jñānāmṛtam anuttamam (non-dual knowledge is unsurpassed nectar); bodhollāsavidhā (method of bliss of awareness) for śivaprāpti (attaining Śiva); yogaśāstra by Kṣemarāja.
unresolved_terms: text has only 2 closing verses (vv. 41–42) — the closing is very brief, almost abrupt
king named Kṣema (rājñaḥ kṣemābhidhānasya) — refers to a patron, not Kṣemarāja himself
text is called a yogaśāstra — a yoga treatise; this is significant: the Bodhavilāsa is not just philosophy but practice
bodh-p05.next_pressure: L2: non-dual knowledge is unsurpassed (v. 41) → whoever drinks it is quenched of saṃsāra-poison → the method of bliss of awareness is for attaining Śiva (v. 42) → the text is a yogaśāstra by Kṣemarāja. Key: v. 41's etad advayam ity uktaṃ jñānāmṛtam anuttamam and v. 42's bodhollāsavidhāneyaṃ śivaprāpyai mahātmanām. Tone: scholastic-practical (yogaśāstra).
